content: Thiabendazole can cause a range of adverse reactions across various organ systems: Gastrointestinal System: Patients may experience loss of appetite (anorexia), nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, discomfort in the upper abdomen (epigastric distress), abdominal pain, jaundice, bile flow obstruction (cholestasis), liver tissue damage (parenchymal liver damage), and in severe cases, liver failure. These effects warrant careful monitoring and adherence to warnings. Central Nervous System: Reported side effects include dizziness, fatigue, drowsiness, a sensation of unsteadiness (giddiness), headaches, numbness, heightened irritability (hyperirritability), seizures (convulsions), episodes of collapse, confusion, depression, a sensation of floating, generalized weakness, and impaired coordination. Special Senses: Adverse effects may involve ringing in the ears (tinnitus), abnormal sensations in the eyes, yellow-tinted vision (xanthopsia), blurred vision, reduced visual acuity, and dryness of mucous membranes, including the mouth and eyes. In some cases, this may progress to Sicca syndrome, a condition characterized by severe dryness. Cardiovascular System: Hypotension (low blood pressure) has been observed as a potential side effect. Metabolic Effects: Hyperglycemia (elevated blood sugar levels) has been reported. Hematologic System: Transient leukopenia (a temporary reduction in white blood cell count) may occur. Genitourinary System: Patients may experience blood in the urine (hematuria), involuntary urination (enuresis), foul-smelling urine, and the presence of crystals in the urine (crystalluria). Hypersensitivity Reactions: These may include itching (pruritus), fever, facial flushing, chills, redness of the eyes (conjunctival injection), swelling of deeper layers of the skin (angioedema), severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), various skin rashes (including those around the anus), erythema multiforme (a skin condition that can include Stevens-Johnson syndrome), and lymph node enlargement (lymphadenopathy). Miscellaneous: In rare cases, live Ascaris worms may appear in the mouth or nose, which can be distressing for the patient. Each of these adverse effects should be carefully considered, and patients should be monitored closely for any signs of these reactions.
